A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same Babel Tower Hypothesis study. The main sections, Algorithm 1, Tables 1-3, Figures 1-9, and Appendices A.1-A.3 can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original multilingual code-model training experiments, internal-state analyses, and original-versus-optimized corpus results, including Table 2 and the appendix figures.

after.justification: v2 retains the work's original training experiments, HumanEval and MBXP results, and checkpoint-based internal-state analyses, including the appendix results.

M1.justification: Equation 2 changes the reported Python-system estimator from (alpha - loss)/(alpha - beta) to (loss - beta)/(alpha - beta). This corrects the quantity used by Algorithm 1 to determine target-language corpus size. The surrounding algorithm and model architecture remain unchanged; changed implementation or reruns are not established.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Python, PHP, C#, Go, and C++ code corpora and the same HumanEval and MBXP tasks. No language, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same StarCoder, StarCoder2, DeepseekCoder, and CodeLlama variants and original-corpus controls. The monolingual comparison models used in Section 3.2 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Equation 2 reverses the reported loss-based internal-state measure used in the Figure 9 validation. This is a metric correction; Pass@1, model sizes, corpus amounts, training budgets, and other stated evaluation procedures remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The corpus-size sensitivity analysis, working-language and neuron analyses, predicted-versus-actual comparisons, and appendix analyses are retained. Appendix A.3 explains the existing validation more explicitly but adds no analysis or evidence beyond the unchanged Figure 9.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the five-checkpoint sliding-window averaging described in Section 4.1.1. Neither adds repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 2 retains every reported value; for example, Optimized-1.3B averages remain 26.61 on HumanEval and 51.97 on MBXP. Figures 2-9 retain the same plotted results, including the appendix curves. The Equation 2 correction is not accompanied by revised results.

T1.justification: Equation 2 receives a mathematical correction: the estimated Python-system proportion now maps the initial and final losses to 1 and 0, respectively, rather than 0 and 1. This matches the stated declining Python-system proportion. Other definitions and equations are unchanged, and no proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same three-stage Babel Tower Hypothesis, internal-state validation claims, and contribution of optimizing multilingual corpus proportions.

C2.justification: The interpretations of language-system transition, cross-language transfer, C++ behavior, and applicability remain unchanged. Appendix A.3 makes the existing working-language proxy explanation more explicit without introducing a new mechanism, limitation, or interpretation of Figure 9.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 now explicitly describes calculating Python working-language proportions at each checkpoint and comparing them with estimates from the corresponding training losses. This adds procedural clarity to the existing validation; it does not establish a changed experiment. Other implementation and access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work discussion are unchanged. Both versions position the contribution as studying multilingual capability development during pre-training, compared with earlier analyses of already-trained models.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites Appendix A.3, updates affiliations and the publication header, adjusts the Babel quotation attribution, and adds an acknowledgments section. The main scientific narrative and section order are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 moves upward within page 3, Figure 9 moves from page 16 to page 15, and Appendix A.3 moves to page 16. Spacing and page breaks also change. The existing figures, captions, and table structures are retained without new graphical evidence.

improvement.justification: The Equation 2 correction resolves an inconsistency between the estimator and the stated decline of the Python system, improving the correctness of the corpus-sizing method as documented. Appendix A.3 also clarifies its validation procedure. These are useful, localized gains; the empirical evidence and broader scientific claims remain unchanged.
